title: A Harbor for the Clock
premise: In 1899, Cyrus Yarrow, a pearl diver's son indentured to the Meridian Trading Company, has survived three years in the harbor town of Saltcross by learning which silences keep people safe. When a census taker presses him about the family that once sheltered him, he realizes his silence could condemn them as declared enemies of the crown. Torn between loyalty to the company that owns his papers and the truth he owes to the woman who saved him, Cyrus must smuggle her son out of the port before the century turns. He succeeds at the cost of his own indenture, choosing exile over invisibility and finally belonging to himself.
about_author: Bram Joubert is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing colonial port records before turning to fiction. His novels explore the quiet bargains ordinary people make with power.

chapters.title: The Weight of Unasked Questions
chapters.summary: Cyrus Yarrow, POV. A census taker arrives at the Meridian Trading Company and asks Cyrus to confirm whether the Ferreira family still occupies the old net-house. Cyrus lies smoothly, but the clerk Halloway notices. The beat is dread: Cyrus understands his three years of careful invisibility have made him valuable precisely because he knows too much.

chapters.title: What the Tide Returned
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV, with an interlude from Marta Ferreira's letters. Cyrus visits Marta in secret and learns her son Tomas is hiding aboard a condemned hulk awaiting deportation. She invokes a promise Cyrus made in peacetime. The emotional beat is guilt sharpening into resolve: loyalty to the company kept him fed; loyalty to her keeps him human.

chapters.title: A Harbor for the Clock
chapters.summary: Cyrus and Halloway alternate POV. Cyrus forges tide-ledger entries to mask a midnight escape while Halloway, suspecting everything, forces a confession-or-betrayal choice. The climax breaks on the water: Cyrus rows Tomas through the patrol lines as the harbor clock strikes the old year out, and Halloway, watching from the quay, chooses not to raise the alarm.

chapters.title: The Century Turns
chapters.summary: Cyrus, POV. Stripped of his indenture and branded a runaway, Cyrus boards a coastal packet with nothing but Marta's gratitude and his own name spoken aloud for the first time in years. The resolution is quiet and earned: belonging was never a place or a master, but the self he stopped hiding. He sails toward an uncertain, honest dawn.
